title: 2010 HMMT November Guts Problem 4
statement: Let \(x\) be a real number. Find the maximum value of \(2^{x(1-x)}\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt[4]{2}\) Consider the function \(2^{y}\). This is monotonically increasing, so to maximize \(2^{y}\), you simply want to maximize \(y\). Here, \(y=x(1-x)=-x^{2}+x\) is a parabola opening downwards. The vertex of the parabola occurs at \(x=(-1) /(-2)=1 / 2\), so the maximum value of the function is \(2^{(1 / 2)(1 / 2)}=\sqrt[4]{2}\).
